Summary:
The data source is an abstract arguing that complex AI methods lead to unintelligible behaviour that threatens trust in mission-critical applications, and that intelligibility can be achieved either through inherently interpretable models or through new explanation techniques such as local approximation, vocabulary alignment and interactive explanation.  We convert these claims into a connected knowledge fabric linking the top-level risk of opaque AI decisions to four concrete interventions that operationalise the recommended approaches.

Report EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[81]
• The abstract is short but fairly explicit, so the extracted reasoning fabric is complete relative to the information provided.  
• Confidence is reduced because only survey-level evidence is mentioned, so several edge confidences are medium or weak.

Inference strategy justification:
Where the paper only lists techniques (e.g. “local approximation”) we inferred a plausible safety-relevant intervention (“apply local surrogate explanation tools during deployment”).  These inferences are marked with confidence level 2 and their rationales cite the Abstract.

Extraction completeness explanation:
All explicit causal relationships (complexity → opacity → need for intelligibility → two solution approaches → concrete mechanisms) are captured.  No isolated nodes exist; every node participates in at least one edge, forming one integrated fabric that branches into four interventions.

Key limitations:
• The abstract provides no quantitative results, so validation evidence is based on a high-level survey statement.  
• Edge direction could be interpreted differently in fuller text.  
• Real implementation detail is sparse; lifecycle and maturity assignments are approximate.
